title: Design a team calendar week view with time-positioned events and an event popover as a layered Figma-ready SVG

Use plain vectors only: no <image>, foreignObject, <script>, CSS animation or external references. Use Inter for all text and the brand color #2563EB.

- Top bar (0, 0, 1440 by 64, with a bottom border): the Tempo logo, a 'Today' button, previous and next chevron buttons, the title 'Sep 21 – 27, 2026', a Day / Week / Month segmented control with Week active, a search field and an avatar.

title: Design light and dark themes of a podcast player screen from one token table as a layered Figma-ready SVG
prompt:
Design the Now playing screen of Pulse, a podcast app, in a light and a dark theme driven by one token table, as one layered SVG file. The canvas is 1160 by 1000 (viewBox 0 0 1160 1000) with a #E9ECF1 background rect. It will be imported into Figma, so organize it like a designer's file: every <g> gets a readable id that becomes its layer name (use ' / ' for hierarchy, never ids like g12), components are nested groups, and all copy stays live <text> (no outlined text). Use plain vectors only: no <image>, foreignObject, <script>, CSS animation or external references. Use Inter for all text.

Tokens (name: light / dark): bg #FFFFFF / #0B0D12; surface #F2F4F7 / #1A1D24; text-primary #101828 / #F5F7FA; text-secondary #667085 / #98A2B3; border #E4E7EC / #2B303B; accent #7C3AED / #A78BFA; on-accent #FFFFFF / #0B0D12; accent-subtle #F4EBFF / #2E2350.

Top-level groups, in this order:
- 'Tokens': a column starting at x 40, y 120 with the title 'Tokens' and eight groups 'Token / <name>', each with a 40 by 40 light swatch and a 40 by 40 dark swatch (rx 8, 1px #D0D5DD stroke) filled with its two values, the token name, and both hex values in uppercase.
- 'Light / Now playing' at x 340, y 120 and 'Dark / Now playing' at x 755, y 120: 375 by 812 frames, each starting with a bg rect in its theme's bg, clipped to the frame, with a 14px label 'Light' or 'Dark' 24px above.

Mirroring: both frames contain the same layers in the same order at the same relative positions and sizes, and every id in the dark frame is the light id with 'Light' replaced by 'Dark' (e.g. 'Light / Now playing / Controls / Play' and 'Dark / Now playing / Controls / Play'). Only colors differ.
Token discipline: apart from the two 'Artwork' groups and the frame labels, every fill and stroke inside a frame must be exactly one of that theme's eight token values (fill='none' is fine), used by role: the screen background is bg; cards and the progress track are surface; titles and times are text-primary; meta text and inactive icons are text-secondary; dividers are border; the play button is accent with an on-accent icon; the progress fill and knob are accent; chips are accent-subtle with accent text. The artwork is identical vector art in both frames.
Screen content, all positions relative to the frame: a status bar with '9:41'; a header with a down chevron, the centered title 'Now playing' and a ⋯ button; 'Artwork', an illustrated podcast cover 311 by 311 with rx 24 at x 32, y 112; the episode title 'The Quiet Power of Routines' (22 bold) and 'Field Notes · Ep. 142'; a 'Progress' group with a 311-wide track at x 32, a fill of exactly 40% of it (124.4) ending in a knob, '18:24' under its left end and '-27:36' under its right end; 'Controls' with 'Button / Rewind 15', 'Button / Play' (a 72 circle centered at x 187.5) and 'Button / Forward 30' at equal distances on either side; a chips row '1.25×', 'Sleep 30 min' and 'Queue'; and an 'Up next' card (surface, rx 16, 311 wide) with a small cover, 'Up next', 'Ep. 143 · Designing for Calm' and '38 min'.

The frames mirror each other: the dark frame has the same descendant ids with 'Light' replaced by 'Dark', in the same order, and at least ten spot-checked elements (artwork, progress track and fill, play button, chips, Up next card, texts) have identical relative positions and sizes.

Token discipline holds: scanning every fill and stroke outside the 'Artwork' groups and frame labels, the light frame uses only #FFFFFF, #F2F4F7, #101828, #667085, #E4E7EC, #7C3AED, #FFFFFF and #F4EBFF, and the dark frame only #0B0D12, #1A1D24, #F5F7FA, #98A2B3, #2B303B, #A78BFA, #0B0D12 and #2E2350 (no stray colors such as #000000 or other grays).

Roles are mapped correctly in both themes: bg background, surface cards and track, text-primary titles and times, text-secondary meta and inactive icons, border dividers, an accent play button with an on-accent icon, an accent progress fill and knob, and accent-subtle chips with accent text.
The 'Tokens' column has eight 'Token / <name>' groups, each with a 40x40 rx 8 light and dark swatch filled with the table values, the token name and both hex values in uppercase matching the table.

Content is exact in both frames: '9:41', 'Now playing', 'The Quiet Power of Routines', 'Field Notes · Ep. 142', '18:24', '-27:36', '1.25×', 'Sleep 30 min', 'Queue', 'Up next', 'Ep. 143 · Designing for Calm' and '38 min', and the progress fill is 124.4 wide (40% of the 311 track, within 1px).

title: Implement a responsive flight results page with a fare calendar, filters, sorting and a trip summary from a Figma file
prompt:
Implement the Skyway flight results page (San Francisco to New York, one way) from our Figma file as a real, responsive, working page. The Figma file is design.json (Figma REST API format). Its page holds two top-level frames, Desktop (1280 wide) and Mobile (390 wide); every node has a descriptive name, an absoluteBoundingBox, fills, strokes, corner radii, effects and, for text, the characters and style. desktop.png and mobile.png are the two frames rendered. Match both frames closely (Inter, the #0b63e5 blue, airline code tiles, tag pills, radii, borders, shadows) and use every string, time and price exactly. Build one responsive page: the Desktop frame from 768px up and the Mobile frame below 768px, using real responsive CSS (flexbox or grid plus media queries), not absolutely positioned boxes. Between 768px and 1280px the desktop layout must adapt without horizontal page scrolling or overlapping text. Use semantic HTML: header with nav, an aside with a filter form (radio inputs for stops, checkboxes for airlines, toggle buttons for the departure-time chips, a range input for max price), main with the fare calendar as a group of buttons, the sort tabs as buttons with aria-pressed or role='tab', and the flights as a list of article cards rendered from one flight data array; the trip summary is an aside. On mobile the search bar collapses into the app bar, the fare calendar scrolls horizontally inside itself, the sort tabs become a segmented control, the filters open from the Filters button, cards become compact, and the trip summary becomes a bar fixed to the bottom of the viewport.

Behavior:
- Fares follow the date: each calendar price is the cheapest fare of that day, and choosing a day shifts every flight's fare by that day's price minus $189 (Thu, Oct 15 is the design). Choosing a day highlights it and updates the heading (e.g. 'Departing flights · Tue, Oct 13'), the Depart field, the 'Fares shown for …' note, the mobile app bar line, every card price, the sort tab summaries and the trip summary. ‹ and › move the selection one day back or forward within the seven days.
- Sort tabs: Best is the design order, Cheapest sorts by fare (low to high), Fastest by duration (short to long). Each tab's second line shows the fare and duration of the flight that would come first in that order among the visible flights.
- Filters combine with AND across groups: Stops (Any number of stops, Nonstop only, 1 stop); Airlines (unchecking hides that airline); Departure time chips that toggle, where several chips combine with OR and none means all (Morning 5:00 AM–11:59 AM, Afternoon 12:00 PM–5:59 PM, Evening 6:00 PM–11:59 PM); and Max price, a slider from $189 to $300 compared with the current fare. The count reads 'Showing N of 8 flights'. When nothing matches, show 'No flights match your filters' with a 'Reset filters' button; it and the panel's Reset restore every filter.
- Exactly one flight is selected (United UA 1532 in the design). Select on another card marks that card Selected and updates Your trip: airline and flight number, date and times, route line, Base fare, 'Taxes & fees (12%)' (12% of the fare, rounded to the cent) and Total; the mobile bottom bar shows the same flight and total. 'Add checked bag' adds $35.00 to the total.
- Mobile: Filters opens a full-screen sheet with the same filters, a close button and a 'Show N flights' button whose N updates live; the segmented control sorts like the tabs.
interaction_hints: Click Cheapest and Fastest and read the card order, then Best. Choose Nonstop only (6 flights; Cheapest tab reads $209 · 5h 26m), then reset. Click the Afternoon chip (DL 418, AA 177, UA 2210), clear it; set the Max price range to 230 (UA 1532, B6 1024, DL 2104, AA 177); uncheck Delta and JetBlue (4 flights); choose 1 stop plus Evening for the empty state and click Reset filters. Click Tue, Oct 13 in the calendar (heading, UA 1532 $215, AA 177 $176, summary $215.00 / $25.80 / $240.80). Back on Thu, Oct 15 click Select on AA 177 (summary $189.00 / $22.68 / $211.68) and toggle Add checked bag ($246.68). Mobile: open Filters, choose Nonstop only, read 'Show 6 flights', close it; use the segmented control. For mobile checks run the interaction helper with --width 390 --height 844; for the intermediate-width check use --width 1024 --height 768 and eval document.documentElement.scrollWidth (must be at most 1024).
